text.title: Carrier invoices against rated shipments
text.lede: Three questions, left to right: did each invoice find a shipment, did the amounts agree, and what happens to it now. The width of a band is the number of invoices taking that route, so the eye follows the volume and then the exceptions peeling away from it.
text.chartTitle: How March’s invoices were paired, judged and dealt with
text.chartSub: Counts of invoices and shipments. Tolerance is 1% or 5.00, whichever is larger. Select a block to follow it.

groups.note: The normal case: an invoice number that matches one shipment.
Split billing: linehaul and accessorials invoiced separately, added up before comparing.
A carrier invoice with no shipment in the transport system.
A delivered shipment the carrier has not invoiced.
The same invoice number received more than once.
Invoiced amount equals the rated amount.
Off by less than the tolerance, usually rounding in the fuel index.
The carrier used last week’s fuel index.
Charges for waiting time, liftgate or redelivery that the shipment record does not support.
The carrier re-weighed the freight and billed a higher class.
No partner on the other side, so no amounts to compare.
Released to payment with no human touch.
Short-pay: the invoice is paid at what the rating says, with a remittance note.
Held, with a query to the carrier.
No invoice yet, so the expected cost is accrued at month end.
